properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on 0.76.0, 0.78.0 and main): the identity file is placed beside the path AS TYPED, not beside the store directory. A store first opened through a symlink gets `<link>.id.json` beside the link. A store opened as `--graph-path .` gets `..id.json` inside itself. Either way `<project>/.reflow2/graph.id.json` is never written, and the next open by the real path is refused as "lost its identity file". That refused open still creates or rewrites graph.meta.json
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-05, triaging art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, entry [defect?] of 2026-10-01: "`bluesky-queueserver/.reflow2/graph.id.json` is missing; `graph.meta.json` was touched today at 13:02. Cause not investigated". This finding is what reflow2 itself can and cannot do. Whether it is what happened on the work machine is not established: see fact:the-bluesky-queueserver-store-lost-its-identity-and-the-work-machine-holds-the-evidence-2026-10-05.

② PRECEDENT: dec:sidecar-loss-guarded-by-store-evidence and fact:defect-lost-identity-sidecar-opens-empty (2026-08-07) made a lost identity a refusal, which the reporter praised. fact:shared-attach-by-absolute-path-missed-the-running-server-and-spawned-a-rival-2026-09-22 is the same class on another sidecar: the rendezvous compared a store's path as typed. That one was fixed. The identity file never was.

③ CANDIDATES for "a store with data and no graph.id.json", read in the code on main f46bd3065 and on v0.76.0:
(a) reflow2 DELETES it. Refuted by reading. The only sidecar deletion is GraphSnapshot::cleanup, which removes `reflow2-snapshot-<pid>.*` in the temp dir. remove_rendezvous and remove_refusal name their own files. The item-layout writer (main only) deletes only nodes/ and edges/ items, and refuses a directory holding foreign files such as graph or graph.id.json. The installer prunes only files its own kit manifest lists. Identical on v0.76.0.
(b) reflow2 truncates it. identity::write uses a plain fs::write, not temp-and-rename, on first open and on a rename (set_label). A kill between truncate and write leaves an EMPTY file. That refuses as "not readable", a different message, so it does not fit the report.
(c) reflow2 NEVER WRITES it beside the real path, because the path was spelled another way. MEASURED (below).
(d) something outside reflow2 parted them: a copy or move of the graph directory alone, a sync tool, `git clean`, a hand rm.

⑤ MEASURED, scratch stores, all three binaries:
- Symlink spelling: proj/.reflow2/graph created empty, stores/bq -> it, one add_requirement through stores/bq. Afterwards stores/ held bq.id.json, bq.meta.json, bq.client.json and bq.usage.jsonl, and proj/.reflow2/ held only graph. get_node by the real path was refused as "lost its identity file" on 0.76.0, 0.78.0 and main. That refused open created proj/.reflow2/graph.meta.json, so the real path ended with exactly the reporter's pair: graph.meta.json present, graph.id.json absent.
- `--graph-path .` from inside the store (0.76.0): the sidecars were written INSIDE the store directory as ..id.json, ..meta.json, ..client.json and ..usage.jsonl.
- A refused open rewrites graph.meta.json: with the id file removed from a working store, one get_node moved graph.meta.json's mtime from 10:57:58 to 10:58:01 on 0.76.0, and likewise on 0.78.0 and main. graph.rs open_rocksdb_with_provenance runs provenance::check_and_stamp before identity::resolve_on_open. Its own comment warns that stamping before a failed open leaves a stray stamp.
- Recovery works: copying the split id file beside the real path, the open succeeded and read the node.

⑥ CLASS: a sidecar is located by the path's spelling rather than by the directory it belongs to. It was fixed for the rendezvous and remains for identity, the version stamp, the client record and the usage ledger (all four followed the symlink spelling above). It is also why a refused open can still leave a fresh sidecar: the open's writes are not ordered after its last refusal.

⑦ NOT DONE (triage only): the pinning test. It would open one store by two spellings (symlink, `.`, relative and absolute) and require one identity.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: which spelling, if any, the work machine used.
